entities.name: Emory University
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia, founded 1836 as Emory College in Oxford, Georgia (named for Methodist bishop John Emory) and relocated to Atlanta in 1915 following a $1 million Candler family gift (the Coca-Cola fortune), is the South's premier research university — home to the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention) partnership as the adjacent federal agency, the Carter Center, one of America's top 10 medical schools, and the Woodruff Library's extraordinary African American history collections. Emory's adjacency to the CDC makes it America's most important institution for public health research training.

Asa Griggs Candler (Coca-Cola founder, Atlanta mayor) and the Candler family donated the 75-acre Druid Hills campus in 1915, transforming a small Methodist college into a major research university. The CDC, established adjacent to Emory in 1946 (originally to combat malaria in the American South), created a unique federal-academic partnership: over 100 CDC scientists hold Emory faculty appointments, and Emory researchers regularly lead CDC outbreak investigation teams. This partnership proved crucial during the 2014 Ebola response and 2020 COVID-19 pandemic.

The Carter Center (established 1982 by former President Jimmy Carter, Emory trustee) is located on Emory's campus, creating an unusual co-location of a former presidential institution with a research university. The Candler School of Theology remains one of America's leading Methodist seminaries. Emory's Winship Cancer Institute and Emory Healthcare system (6,000+ physicians) make it Atlanta's dominant healthcare provider.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Emory University's CDC adjacency and partnership — making it America's premier public health research university — proved consequential during both the 2014 Ebola outbreak and 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, demonstrating how geographic proximity between federal agencies and universities can create outsized global public health impact.
